projects.title: Order & Inventory Operations Workbench
projects.summary: Modular React + TypeScript interface for tracking fulfillment queues, SLA thresholds, and stock movements with instant multi-column filtering.
projects.description:
Designed around lessons learned building production React frontends: operators need fast keyboard navigation, URL-synced filters, and zero layout shift when switching status queues.

The interface separates filter state from table rendering so 1,000+ order rows filter smoothly without redundant re-renders. Includes inline status inspection, SLA breach indicators, and CSV export for downstream reporting.

projects.title: Retail Cohort & Margin Telemetry
projects.summary: End-to-end SQL and Power BI analysis of 48,900+ retail transactions uncovering repeat-buyer retention drivers and SKU margin concentration.
projects.description:
Raw transactional exports often hide profitability problems behind rising gross revenue. In this analysis, I cleaned multi-month order logs using Python and SQL CTEs, deduplicated customer identifiers, and modeled monthly retention cohorts alongside SKU-level net margin.

The resulting dashboard pairs cohort heatmaps with a Pareto margin breakdown so merchandising teams can spot high-return product lines versus discount-heavy volume traps.

insights.label: 90-day repeat rate
insights.detail: Customers whose second order occurred within 21 days retained at 2.4x the baseline rate.

insights.label: Pareto margin share
insights.detail: Less than one-fifth of catalog items generated 71% of net contribution margin after discounts.

insights.label: Promo margin leakage
insights.detail: Sitewide voucher campaigns lifted order count but compressed net margin on core staples.

projects.title: Teacher & Student Grade Portal
projects.summary: Role-based academic portal built with Java and MySQL enabling faculty to manage student records while giving students read-only grade visibility.
projects.description:
Built to replace error-prone manual grade sheets with a structured relational database and graphical desktop interface. Teachers authenticate into a management view where they can register student records, encode term grades, and update contact details.

Students log into a restricted read-only view scoped strictly to their own academic standing. Backed by a normalized MySQL schema enforcing student ID constraints and audit-ready record lookups.

projects.title: Huffman Tree Compression & Bit Telemetry
projects.summary: Lossless file compression utility in C++ using character frequency distributions, priority queues, and binary Huffman trees to shrink text payloads.
projects.description:
Developed collaboratively to study how statistical character distributions directly reduce storage footprint. The engine scans input files to build a frequency table, constructs a min-heap priority queue, and derives optimal prefix-free binary codes via a Huffman tree.

During execution, the CLI outputs complete bit-level telemetry—character frequencies, padded binary streams, compressed byte counts, and exact execution time—verifying zero data loss upon decompression.

insights.label: Payload bit reduction
insights.detail: High-skew English text strings compressed to roughly half their fixed 8-bit ASCII bit length.

insights.label: Decode verification
insights.detail: Sub-second tree reconstruction and bit-padding removal with 100% lossless round-trip parity.

projects.title: Hardware-Token ATM Banking System
projects.summary: C++ banking workflow simulation that uses a physical USB flash drive as an encrypted ATM card for balance inquiries, transfers, and PIN management.
projects.description:
Models end-to-end automated teller workflows including account creation, balance checks, deposits, withdrawals, cash transfers, and PIN updates.

Instead of typing an account number manually, the system detects an inserted USB drive acting as the user's physical bank card and verifies an encrypted PIN file stored on the volume before unlocking ledger transactions.

posts.title: From Raw SQL Tables to Honest KPIs: Cleaning Data Before Charting It
posts.excerpt: Why dashboard accuracy is won or lost in the SQL layer—using CTEs, deduplication, and window functions before opening Power BI or Python.
posts.content:
A polished Power BI or Tableau chart cannot rescue an unverified denominator. Whenever I start exploring a dataset—whether academic records in MySQL or multi-month retail order logs—I try to answer three questions in plain SQL before touching a visual chart.

## Step 1: Audit duplicates and status flags first

Real exports almost always include retried webhooks, cancelled checkouts, or test accounts. Summing `amount` directly inflates revenue by 5% to 15%.

```sql
WITH deduplicated_orders AS (
  SELECT
    order_id,
    customer_id,
    created_at,
    net_amount,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY order_id
      ORDER BY updated_at DESC
    ) AS row_num
  FROM raw_orders
  WHERE order_status IN ('COMPLETED', 'SHIPPED')
    AND customer_email NOT LIKE '%@test.internal'
)
SELECT
  DATE_FORMAT(created_at, '%Y-%m-01') AS order_month,
  COUNT(order_id) AS valid_orders,
  ROUND(SUM(net_amount), 2) AS net_revenue
FROM deduplicated_orders
WHERE row_num = 1
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
```

Using `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ...)` guarantees each order is counted once, even if an upstream ingestion script appended duplicate status rows.

## Step 2: Pair averages with distributions

Reporting only an "Average Order Value" of ₱1,450 hides whether most customers spend ₱1,400 or whether a handful of wholesale buyers mask a ₱450 retail median.

| Metric | Raw Export | Cleaned Cohort | Why It Matters |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Gross Orders | 52,140 | 48,920 | Removes 3,220 cancelled & duplicate rows |
| Mean Order Value | ₱1,510 | ₱1,425 | Reflects settled net revenue |
| Median Order Value | ₱980 | ₱960 | Anchors realistic promo thresholds |

## Step 3: Let visuals highlight the decision, not decorate the page

When bringing cleaned tables into Power BI, Excel, or a custom React SVG chart:

1. **Reserve color for signal.** Keep gridlines and axes quiet so a single warm accent draws the eye directly to the threshold or cohort shift that needs attention.
2. **Show deltas alongside absolutes.** "34.8% 90-day retention (+6.2 pts YoY)" gives immediate context; a lone number without a baseline forces the reader to guess whether it is healthy.
3. **Document your metric definitions.** Writing a two-line tooltip explaining how a KPI is calculated builds instant trust with both engineers and business stakeholders.
